Process_Description: UK Type G 230V 50Hz mains feeds the Main PC (Windows 11, i9, RTX 4080), which also supplies 5V USB bus power to the ELEGOO Mega R3, Focusrite Scarlett 2i2, and ToF sensor.
UK Type G 230V 50Hz mains feeds the Beetronics 22HB9M/U1 external AC-to-DC power adapter for the 22-inch high-brightness display.
UK Type G 230V 50Hz mains feeds the Mean Well LPV-150-24 LED driver (~89% efficiency; 120W safe continuous DC output / 150W max).
Mean Well LPV-150-24 outputs regulated 24V DC to the 3000K WS2814 COB RGBW LED strips (V- bonded to Arduino Mega GND).
UK Type G 230V 50Hz mains feeds the dedicated 24V DC auxiliary power supply driving both TCD-180M card dispensers.
Dedicated 24V DC power rail feeds the TCD-180M Plastic Card Dispenser motor and logic board.
Dedicated 24V DC power rail feeds the TCD-180M Metal Card Dispenser motor and logic board.
UK Type G 230V 50Hz mains feeds the dedicated 5V DC power supply for the 6121 TMC2209 stepper driver.
Dedicated 5V DC power supply feeds the 6121 TMC2209 stepper motor driver (common GND bonded to Arduino Mega GND; verify VM >= 4.75V under load).
UK Type G 230V 50Hz mains feeds the Fosi Audio V3 32V/5A power supply driving the Dayton BST-1 shaker on one channel (capped at 50W RMS).
UK Type G 230V 50Hz mains directly powers the active Genelec 8010A mono studio monitor (internal 25W+25W Class D amp).
Main PC GPU outputs the HTML Frontend idle attract screen to the Beetronics 22HB9M/U1 high-brightness outdoor display over HDMI or DisplayPort.
HTML Frontend sends idle lighting state command to Python Hardware Controller over localhost.
Python Hardware Controller reads idle animation parameters from the local LED CSV config and sends a state activation packet to ELEGOO Mega R3 over USB-A to USB-B serial.
Arduino Mega drives 3000K 24V COB RGBW WS2814 strips using the Adafruit NeoPixel library (1-wire NRZ data via 330-470 ohm resistor) powered by the Mean Well LPV-150-24 PSU.
User taps an interactive control on the Beetronics 22HB9M/U1 touchscreen; touch coordinates are sent to the Main PC and HTML Frontend over USB HID.
HTML Frontend processes the touch input and renders the updated interface screen back to the Beetronics 22HB9M/U1 over HDMI or DisplayPort.
HTML Frontend sends a new lighting state command (e.g. processing / win / alert) to Python Hardware Controller.
Python Hardware Controller maps the requested state from the LED animation CSV and sends a compact state-switch command to ELEGOO Mega R3 over USB serial.
Arduino Mega smoothly transitions the 24V WS2814 COB RGBW LED strips to the new animation profile via Adafruit NeoPixel (1-wire NRZ protocol).
User taps the start button on the Beetronics 22HB9M/U1 touchscreen; USB touch event is received by the HTML Frontend.
HTML Frontend sends dispense command for a plastic card to Python Hardware Controller.
Python Hardware Controller communicates directly with the TCD-180M Plastic Card Dispenser over its dedicated wired USB serial COM port to eject one plastic card.
TCD-180M Plastic Card Dispenser confirms successful ejection (or reports low / empty hopper or jam) back over wired USB serial.
Python Hardware Controller relays dispense confirmation to HTML Frontend to advance the user journey.
HTML Frontend updates the Beetronics 22HB9M/U1 display over HDMI or DisplayPort to prompt the user to collect their plastic card.
Card acceptor Time-of-Flight (ToF) sensor detects an inserted plastic card at the intake slot and reports distance drop to ELEGOO Mega R3 over I2C.
Arduino Mega briefly pauses LED interrupts and outputs STEP/DIR/EN pulses to the 6121 TMC2209 Stepper Driver to pull the card into the machine.
6121 TMC2209 Stepper Driver (powered by its dedicated 5V PSU) energizes the bipolar stepper coils to rotate the intake rollers until the card is seated.
Arduino Mega transmits card-inserted activation state to Python Hardware Controller via USB-A to USB-B wired serial comms.
Python Hardware Controller relays the card-inserted event to HTML Frontend.
HTML Frontend renders the post-insertion screen onto the Beetronics 22HB9M/U1 monitor over HDMI or DisplayPort.
HTML Frontend sends vibration trigger to Python Hardware Controller with intensity (1 to 5) and duration (ms) values.
Python Hardware Controller generates a band-limited 20-60 Hz waveform scaled to intensity 1-5 and streams it strictly to Channel 1 (Left) of the Focusrite Scarlett 2i2 in shared audio mode.
Focusrite Scarlett 2i2 routes Channel 1 via Line Out 1 using a 1/4-inch TS unbalanced cable into the Left RCA input of the Fosi Audio V3.
Fosi Audio V3 (32V version, single channel only and gain-capped for 50W) amplifies the signal over speaker wire to vibrate the Dayton Audio BST-1 mounted to the cash machine frame.
HTML Frontend generates UI/SFX audio directly and routes it straight to Channel 2 (Right) of the PC's connected audio interface (Focusrite Scarlett 2i2), bypassing the Python Hardware Controller.
Focusrite Scarlett 2i2 outputs balanced mono line audio from Line Out 2 via a 1/4-inch TRS to Male XLR cable directly into the AC-powered Genelec 8010A speaker.
User taps the metal card dispense prompt on the Beetronics 22HB9M/U1 touchscreen; USB HID touch input triggers the HTML Frontend.
HTML Frontend sends dispense command for a metal card to Python Hardware Controller.
Python Hardware Controller communicates directly with the TCD-180M Metal Card Dispenser over its dedicated wired USB serial COM port to eject one metal card.
TCD-180M Metal Card Dispenser confirms ejection (or flags heavy-card slip / jam / empty hopper) back to Python over wired USB serial.
Python Hardware Controller updates HTML Frontend that the metal card has been dispensed.
HTML Frontend updates the Beetronics 22HB9M/U1 display over HDMI or DisplayPort to prompt the user to collect their metal card.
TCD-180M Metal Card Dispenser detects a card jam or empty hopper during a dispense attempt and returns an error status code over wired USB serial.
Python Hardware Controller sends error lighting state command to ELEGOO Mega R3 over USB serial.
Arduino Mega switches WS2814 COB RGBW LED strips via Adafruit NeoPixel to an error indicator state.
Python Hardware Controller notifies HTML Frontend with the dispenser fault code to lock out normal operation.
HTML Frontend displays an out-of-service / technician alert message on the Beetronics 22HB9M/U1 touchscreen over HDMI or DisplayPort.
